recipes.name: Voodoo Pasta
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package Hillshire Farm® Smoked Sausage
1 teaspoon hot sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Cook pasta according to package directions; drain.
While pasta is cooking, cut sausage into 1/4-inch-thick slices. Place in a bowl and sprinkle with seasoning; toss lightly to evenly coat.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Add sausage; cook and stir for 3 to 4 minutes or until lightly browned. Stir in Alfredo sauce, parsley, and hot sauce to taste; heat through.
Pour sauce over pasta and toss until well coated. Serve immediately.

raw_recipe.headline: Voodoo Pasta
raw_recipe.description: Voodoo pasta is ready as quickly as the fusilli cooks. Make a spicy Alfredo sauce with blackened smoked sausage, and when the pasta is done, just toss everything together. It's pure magic.

review.reviewBody: YUMMMMM! Absolutely delicious. I haven't been able to taste alfredo in 6 years due to a car accident (its usually too weak tasting). But this is just perfect. Its sooo good. Just a suggestion... use Tony Chachere's for the cajun spice.

I’m not a spice person so I used the Cajun seasoning for a milder flavor and no hot sauce but added pepper. Was delicious. Don’t know why people review a recipe that doesn’t appeal to them in the first place. Make your own Alfredo sauce or just skip the recipe altogether. Not all recipes appeal to me so I just don’t comment!

First time making this dish for the family. They loved it! Followed directions (with small exceptions) and this can be from fridge to table in 20 mins and that's just because you're boiling the pasta separately here. Only things I changed was after I added the Alfredo sauce jar, I filled it with about a cup and a half heavy cream, 1 egg yolk, fresh salt and pepper and put the lid on right for a good shake. Poured that into sauce to add more flavor, thickener and volume (I like more sauce). I also added slivered garlic and a little minced shallot to the sausage just before adding the Alfredo to add more depth of flavor. Was awesome! Next time I might slice the sausage casings off, saute the sausage and crumble it into the sauce instead so I can also add either chicken, shrimp, or some other protein to really take it to another level!
It was good but why pre-season the sausage with salt? I skipped that as sausage is already over salted.
I used real grated Parmesan cheese 🧀 along with a jar of Alfredo sauce and it got a little thicker and creamier. 😋

Very easy to make and can be made very spicy. I substituted smoked Andouille sausage for the smoked sausage. Then i used homemade Alfredo sauce. 2 cups whipping cream, 2 Tbsp butter: simmer 15 minutes; then add 1 cup parmesan cheese.
Very good but I added and don’t understand why garlic and the holy trinity weren’t added to this recipe. Much better with it.

I thought it was too salty with the smoked sausage. I tried two times to make it work with that, but the family was overwhelmed with the salt. So I changed it to sauteing mild italian sausage in its casing, cut into small rounds. When that was browned, I transferred to another pan. In the same pan with all the drippings, I sauteed a chopped shallot and 5 cloves of minced garlic. Added the sausage back. Switched from fusilli to penne. Used a vodka sauce. Chopped parsley and parmesan on top.

This has become a favorite at my house. I do tweak it: Rao’s Alfredo only if you don’t make your own. Rao’s fusilli pasta. I use twice the amount of sausage. I brown it with one onion and wipe out a lot of the grease before continuing. I also add fresh garlic or frozen minced garlic (2-3 cloves). I use more seasonings than it calls for because I make more sauce. To do this I add the entire jar of Rao’s, then fill it about halfway with heavy cream. Shake it up and pour over the sausage/onion mixture. Then add shredded parm (just cover the top of the skillet) and mix. I also add black pepper. Next I add cherry tomatoes (cut in half) and mix. Serve topped with chopped green onion. Fabulous!

It’s good, but I also sautéed an onion with the sausage, and then added some fresh garlic until it was fragrant. Once the alfredo sauce was added ( I used knorrs mix with milk) I stirred in some julienne sun dried tomato and baby spinach. Top with fresh parm. Spectacular!

This was so simple and easy to whip up. Everyone literally licked their plate clean! I took it a couple steps further by sautéing fine diced shallots, garlic and a handful of fresh chopped roma tomatoes in the same pan I browned the sausage in before putting it all together.
Sauce was too salty certain the hot sauce contributed. Cut it with a good pinch of sugar and turned out quite tasty.
Really good dinner when there's no time for long prep in the kitchen and all you want is to feed your family and get in comfy clothes! The whole family agreed its a keeper

It was ok. I regret my decision to use turkey sausage. The parsley tasted like it should have been basil. I think that it would benefit from something that would add depth like onions, spinach or sun-dried tomatoes. Also, I thought it could use to be spicier. That could have been my spices that were not strong enough.
Omit sausage. Make my own Alfredo pasta sauce.

This recipe is nice and easy to make. I did use a different shaped pasta because that's what I had on hand, but it was a shape that holds sauces well. I used Rao's Alfredo sauce, Hillshire Farm smoked beef sausage, Slap Ya' Mama Cajun seasoning, and Frank's Red Hot for the couple of shots of hot sauce. I cooked 12 oz pasta and the beef sausage was a 12 oz sausage but all other ingredients were as per the recipe. I did thin the sauce out with some pasta water as it was very thick and my pasta was thick and al dente when I moved it into the pan. Flavor of dish was addictive and very filling. I had to force myself to stop eating it.
Followed recipe except used dried parsley. Turned out great!
This is so flavorful. I thought I had hot sauce, but didn’t so I added 1/4 tsp of Cayenne pepper. Soooooo yummy!!!

I made just 2 changes. I thought I had some Alfredo sauce & didn't so I used a can of cream of mushroom soup adding about 1/4 cup of the pasta water to thin it down some. I also left out the hot sauce. This can be made with ground beef, chicken & even shrimp which are some of the changes I'll be making in the very near future. This is delicious and so easy.
I just made this and it's going on repeat! I stepped it up by making my own Alfredo sauce! 😋
